Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About the Role

We're seeking a detail-oriented Office Coordinator to support our Workplace team and be the heartbeat of our NYC office operations. This person will report into the current Office Manager. As the first face visitors see and the go-to person for our team's daily needs, you'll create an environment where creativity and productivity thrive. This role combines the precision of facilities management with the warmth of hospitality.

The ideal candidate thrives in a dynamic environment where no two days are the same, bringing both meticulous organizational skills and a natural talent for making people feel welcome. From managing confidential documents to coordinating team experiences, your attention to detail and proactive approach will ensure our workplace supports our team's best work.

Listen to the song we made about the role! https://suno.com/s/Xvlkl9u53fQxJzIq

What You’ll Do

Administrative Management:

  • Process and maintain NDAs, waivers, and contracts

  • Serve as onsite coordinator for guests and candidates

  • Handle incoming/outgoing package shipments

  • Scan and distribute incoming mail to appropriate teams

  • Manage digital and physical filing systems

  • Serve as primary point of contact for vendors and service providers

  • Establish and negotiate partnerships with local hotels and vendors

  • Support visiting executives and special projects

Office Operations & Facilities:

  • Oversee office maintenance and promptly address facility issues

  • Maintain daily office cleanliness and organization

  • Manage security system including badges and camera monitoring

  • Manage onsite music studio, support partnerships team in hosting artists

  • Provide plant care and maintenance throughout the office

  • Monitor and stock food/beverage supplies

  • Coordinate daily lunch program including setup, service, and cleanup

  • Maintain office supply inventory

  • Process incoming and outgoing mail/packages

  • Manage guest and visitor access, including registration with building security

  • Oversee AV systems setup and troubleshooting

  • Coordinate device procurement and inventory

Team Experience:

  • Plan and execute team events and activities

  • Create a welcoming environment for employees and visitors

  • Support office culture initiatives

  • Support the talent acquisition team through onsite coordination

  • Support new hire onboarding

What You’ll Need

  • 1-2 years of experience in office management or facilities coordination

  • Strong organizational and multitasking abilities

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills

  • Experience managing vendor relationships

  • Proficiency with office management software and digital tools

  • Problem-solving mindset with ability to work independently

  • Detail-oriented approach with a proactive attitude

  • Comfort with dynamic environments and changing priorities

  • A love of music is a huge plus

Additional Notes:

  • Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

  • This is an in person role working at our NYC office

  • This is a 3 month contract with the possibility to extend or convert to full time

 

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.title: Senior / Staff Data Scientist, Trust & Safety
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About the Role

Trust should be the foundation of every relationship Suno has — with our users, our artists, our rightsholders, and the broader music community. We're looking for our first dedicated data scientist on the Trust & Safety team to help make that real by building the metrics and analysis that let us measure how we're doing, and collaborating to define and execute on an impactful roadmap. You'll partner closely with product, engineering, and legal to bring a rigorous, quantitative lens to problems like copyright detection, content filtering, and bot detection. You and cross-functional stakeholders will work together to create a seamless creative environment for our users that is built on security and trust.

Listen to the song we made about the role: https://suno.com/s/ip8Q3TIlQxuaTyOt

What You'll Do

  • Define and evaluate metrics for the health of our trust and safety ecosystem

  • Analyze and build models, algorithms, and methodologies for maintaining a safe platform, like bot detection, content filtering, copyright detection, etc.

  • Design and run experiments that measure the real impact of changes to Trust & Safety practices, and turn results into clear recommendations

  • Partner with product and engineering to size opportunities and shape the Trust & Safety roadmap

  • Contribute to building strong data foundations as part of our awesome data science team

What You'll Need

Must-Haves

  • 6–8 years of experience in data science or a closely related analytical field, with several years in trust & safety or closely adjacent problems (e.g., spam/fraud, integrity, policy-adjacent ML)

  • Strong hands-on SQL and Python

  • Experience running online experiments end-to-end, from ideation and metrics selection through analysis and informing the final decision

  • Experience building metrics or evaluation frameworks from scratch, without established precedent to lean on

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience training and building predictive ML models, offline and real-time.

  • Musician or creative hobbyist

Work Location Policy

This role is expected to work from the designated Suno office 5 days a week, per Suno's company policy. Full-time employees will receive competitive equity packages, and comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered may vary depending on location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

Additional Notes

Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

Founded in 2023 by Harvard alumni with a shared passion for music, Suno has quickly grown to 250 employees while empowering more than 100 million people to create original songs. In 2026, we raised a $400 million Series D at a $5.4 billion valuation to continue building innovative products that amplify creativity and imagination.

About the Role

The Manager, Music Marketing is a mid-level role responsible for working within the team that shapes how the world discovers, experiences, creates and connects with music on Suno.

The ideal candidate is a creative marketer who understands how audiences are discovering and engaging with music online and IRL. You’ll be part of the artist & music marketing team that shapes the marketing programs we’re creating in partnership with the industry. You’ll also be responsible for the ideation and execution of the marketing campaigns that help fans connect with the music and artists on Suno.

This role reports to the Head of Artist Marketing & Editorial and sits across music, marketing, product, and the Suno brand, making it a uniquely high-impact seat at a company redefining what music creation can be.

Listen to the song we made about the role! https://suno.com/s/oinhIznaWyP1bo3W

What You’ll Do

  • Own the overall strategy and performance of artist marketing campaigns, ensuring consistent pipeline, quality execution, and measurable impact

  • Own the A to Z of a campaign ensuring that it’s a success for the artist, the fans, and Suno

  • Make cool things happen for artists who are making music with Suno

  • Make cool things happen for artists delivering their music on Suno to be remixed and interacted with

  • Challenge and help define what artist and music marketing looks like at a music creation and music interaction platform - we are not a DSP and we are not a label

  • Work with the marketing, editorial, comms, creative and brand teams to find and build the pipelines and programs that support artists, creative community, and the industry

  • Work cross-functionally with the growth, product and brand teams to represent the artist community in product launches

  • Create new opportunities (on and off platform) for music and artists on Suno

  • Serve as an escalation point and senior relationship holder for high-priority industry and artist partnerships and their representatives

  • Establish and maintain best practices around campaign operations, including data analysis, rights clearances, contracting, cross-functional coordination, and performance reporting

  • Partner with Legal and Finance to ensure all artist agreements and payments are handled with rigor and care

  • Collaborate within the artist & music marketing team to disrupt and redefine what artist marketing and music consumptions looks like in 2026 and beyond

  • Own success and metrics reporting, including campaign performance, reach, and remix metrics

What You’ll Need

Required Experience & Expertise

  • 8-10 years of experience having worked in the music and entertainment industries, preferably from a DSP, management or record label.

  • Experience working with talent is a must, with a deep sensitivity and empathy to working with artists and handling their creative projects and outputs

  • A creative brain

  • You’re a builder and maker, not just a facilitator

  • Deep familiarity with music industry structures including recording, publishing, and representation agreements, and how they affect partnership and campaign execution

  • Experience ideating, executing and managing end-to-end artist marketing campaigns with cross-functional stakeholders and complex logistics

  • Relationships with artists, managers, and various stakeholders in the music industry

  • Excellent communicator: able to represent Suno credibly with senior artist teams and external partners, and communicate clearly and directly internally

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and energized by the pace and possibility of a high-growth environment

  • Passion for music and sincere belief in technology's potential to expand creative access and expression

  • A thirst for music culture

Preferred

  • Experience at a music technology, streaming, or AI company

  • Experience working within or alongside product and engineering teams

Additional Notes:

  • Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

  • This role requires working on-site in Los Angeles (Venice Beach).

Compensation:

The annual salary range for this role is $160,000 – $210,000

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees:

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. About the Role

Suno is standing up an Artists & Creators pod, and our first major focus is Songkick.com — our newly acquired live music and ticketing product. We're hiring an early team to take technical ownership of Songkick within Suno across the stack: the backend, the website, the mobile app, the data pipelines, and the notification systems that power it. You'll report to the Songkick Engineering Manager and work closely with the Songkick General Manager, our Product Manager, and our Music teams to help define how this team tracks success and grows. Early on, the work is hands-on and diverse — understanding the existing system deeply, stabilizing it, and finding the integration points that make Songkick and Suno stronger together. Over time, this role has real influence over the roadmap, engineering best practices, and leaving a handprint on Suno's Artists & Creators engineering team.

Check out the Suno version of the role here! https://suno.com/s/emzEA5oPeNN6dxK2

What You'll Do

  • Own part of the Songkick product end-to-end, wherever you’re strongest — from backend, mobile app (React Native, iOS + Android), data pipelines, and notifications

  • Lead the technical integration of Songkick into Suno, partnering with the Songkick Engineering Manager, Product Manager, incoming General Manager, and our existing engineering team to identify what to build next

  • Architect and maintain data aggregation systems that ingest, normalize, and score touring and event data from dozens of sources into a single canonical record

  • Assess a large, established codebase and make clear-eyed calls about what to preserve, modernize, or retire

  • Design APIs consumed by mobile clients, working directly with the teams building on top of them

  • Extend Suno's mission of making creative fulfillment a daily reality into how fans discover and experience live music

What You'll Need

Must-Haves

  • 5–10 years of software engineering experience, with a demonstrated hunger to stay close to the code and the end user

  • An ownership mentality — you enjoy taking a large, ambiguous product space and running with it end-to-end

  • Startup experience shipping quickly in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment

  • Strong API design skills, having worked closely with iOS/Android or other mobile teams

  • A flexible set of communication styles — you reduce entropy rather than create it, pride yourself on your ability to write, as well as facilitate live discussions with stakeholders ranging in level of technical expertise

  • Experience working with modern agentic coding workflows, including E2E testing harnesses, reusable skills, and defining clear success criteria

  • Enthusiasm for rapid learning, regardless of whether technology and tools are brand new or legacy

  • A preference for deeply collaborative environments

Experience with a few of the following:

  • Experience building systems that ingest data from 20+ sources, normalize it, score or weight it by source reliability, apply survivorship rules, and store a canonical record

  • Strong SQL and NoSQL experience

  • Strong data modeling and system architecture skills at scale

  • Tuning Web, Android, and/or iOS performance metrics with a healthy fear of red numbers

  • Building out a design system to accelerate development whilst keeping a consistent feel

  • Experience retrofitting design systems

Nice-to-Haves

  • Hands-on experience with React Native and/or Ruby on Rails

  • Experience building or maintaining email or push notification systems

This Role is a Match for Candidates Who:

  • Thrive in ambiguous, fast-paced environments — you don't need everything mapped out to move forward

  • Bring low ego and high versatility, equally at ease debugging a small fix or driving a major project

  • Get energy from rapid prototyping and iteration — you'd rather ship something rough and refine it than wait for perfect

  • Have a genuine passion for music and live events, and want that passion reflected in your work

Additional Notes:

  • Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

  • This is an in-person role working at our Cambridge, NYC, LA offices.

 

Perks & Benefits

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

 

Compensation

The annual salary range for this role is $ $228K-$363K + target equity + benefits (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

Founded in 2023 by Harvard alumni with a shared passion for music, Suno has quickly grown to 200 employees while empowering more than 100 million people to create original songs. In 2026, we raised a $400 million Series D at a $5.4 billion valuation to continue building innovative products that amplify creativity and imagination.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Paid Social Manager who is a true specialist in paid social performance marketing. You’ll manage our paid social campaigns end-to-end: platform partnerships, testing and measurement, driving web and app conversions at scale across markets.

This is a role for someone who has done this at real scale: you've managed paid social budgets of $30M+ annually, you understand attribution deeply, and you bring rigor, curiosity, and sharp analytical instincts to everything you touch. You should be comfortable digging into the data yourself — building your own analyses, spotting issues before anyone asks, and translating numbers into clear action. If that sounds like you, you'll fit right in.

You're also a builder, not just an operator. When a workflow is slow or a test framework doesn't exist yet, you build it rather than waiting for someone else to. You think like a creator: better tests, sharper creative, smarter systems. If that sounds like you, you'll fit right in.

We made a song about the role: https://suno.com/s/owdc28Zl5z3YqWbN

What You’ll Do

  • Own Paid Social channel performance globally: manage campaigns optimizing for web and app conversions, subscriptions, and growth KPIs across multiple geographies and markets. Evaluate and pilot new platforms and formats as they become relevant.

  • Drive full-funnel results: manage budgets, bidding strategies, audience segmentation, and creative testing to consistently hit CPA and ROAS targets at scale

  • Manage platform partnerships: own the relationship with paid social channel reps, including beta access, product roadmap input, billing, and spend reconciliation.

  • Own analysis and reporting: run proactive weekly performance analyses, using Excel and other tools to diagnose trends and surface opportunities. Design and run incrementality tests (geo holdouts, lift studies) to confirm spend is driving net new users, not just capturing demand that would have converted anyway.

  • Navigate app campaign complexity: own tracking setup (Conversions API), MMP integration (Singular, AppsFlyer, Adjust, etc.), and mobile attribution nuance across platforms

  • Build your own tools: when something is broken or needs improvement, build the fix yourself. Write the script, build the dashboard, design the smarter test framework. You do not wait for someone else to solve it, and you use your best judgement and expertise to make sure the analysis, strategy and execution drives excellent results.

  • Partner with creative & across the business: own all creative analysis and give structured feedback on ad creative, brief new concepts, and drive iteration based on performance data. Work with lifecycle/CRM, product, data science, and finance to align on audience strategy, budget, and measurement.

  • Own budget and forecasting: manage pacing across campaigns and markets, proactively reallocating spend to what’s working

  • Communicate with clarity: translate complex campaign data into sharp insights and recommendations for cross-functional stakeholders

Qualifications

  • 3+ years hands-on managing conversion-optimized paid social campaigns (must have specific paid social channel experience) with multi-million annual budget responsibility across major platforms

  • Strong grasp of web conversion campaigns — pixels, events, landing page performance, and full-funnel optimization

  • Experience running global campaigns across multiple geographies and markets

  • Experience with app campaign mechanics and mobile attribution (MMPs like Singular, AppsFlyer, Adjust; SKAdNetwork, postbacks, etc.)

  • Sharp analytical skills: advanced in Excel, including pivot tables, with a track record of proactively running weekly and ad hoc analyses to diagnose performance and drive decisions — not just reporting on results, but getting ahead of them

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where channels, tools, and strategy evolve constantly

  • Nice to have: experience across a broad range of paid channels beyond the major social platforms (such as, X, Snapchat, Pinterest)

Additional Notes

  • Must be eligible to work in the US.

  • Must be willing to work 5 days/week in-office.

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Compensation

Base salary: $145,000 – $170,000 (before equity)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.title: Director, Trust & Safety
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

The role

You will lead Trust & Safety at Suno. Directly leading enforcement operations and policy, you will also partner with PM, Eng, and Legal to scale detection and remediation of violative content, fraud, bots, and identity issues, while also navigating music rights and our regulatory obligations. Generation volume grows faster than any human review model can, so we focus on building enforcement systems that scale with the platform, hold it to a high degree of accuracy, and know exactly what decisions costs. You will report to the Head of Operations and partner regularly with Comms, Product, Engineering, ML, and Legal.

Listen to the song we made about the role: https://suno.com/s/QawvJRO3jhDr1Cb8

What you'll do

  • Build and lead the T&S team, including enforcement operations, policy, vendor programs, quality management, and training.

  • Own enforcement economics end-to-end: cost per decision, precision and recall tradeoffs at volume, automation rate targets, queue design, and the vendor versus in-house mix.

  • Govern AI-assisted decisioning: model-assisted enforcement pipelines, human-in-the-loop thresholds, appeals architecture, and audit accountability for automated actions.

  • Own the BPO relationship and every Trust & Safety vendor partnership: selection, contract negotiation support, capacity strategy, quality accountability, and the decision of what stays outsourced versus moves in-house

  • Run the operational layer of music rights enforcement: rights-matching abuse patterns, impersonation and copyright workflows, in close partnership with Legal.

  • Partner with Legal to translate regulatory regimes (DSA, OSA and emerging AI-content rules) into tooling, process and measurable operational readiness.

  • Represent Trust & Safety to executive leadership with clear metrics and honest tradeoffs.

What you'll bring

  • 8+ years in trust & safety, integrity, or content operations, including 4+ years leading teams through significant scale inflections.

  • Demonstrated ownership of enforcement metrics at a UGC or generative AI platform: automation rate, decision accuracy, cost per action, appeal overturn rate.

  • Experience building or governing model-assisted enforcement with human-in-the-loop design and audit accountability.

  • A track record of moving Product, Engineering, Legal, and Policy without direct authority.

Nice to have

  • Music, media or IP-adjacent platform experience and fluency in rights-matching abuse patterns.

  • Direct exposure to DSA, OSA or emerging AI-content regulatory regimes as operational requirements.

Compensation and benefits

The annual salary range for this role is $195,200 - $256,200 + target equity + benefits (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

About the Role

We’re hiring an Engineering Manager to lead Suno’s Social team — a small, high-caliber group of fullstack product engineers building the network effects that turn Suno from a single-player creation tool into a creative network. You’ll own the team’s talent, delivery, and technical direction across the social layer: organic notifications, profiles and creative identity, the follow graph, and social engagement from sharing to comments. This is a hands-on leadership role — you’ll grow the team, set the technical bar by example, and partner closely with product, design, and data science to discover what social means for music. The charter is still expanding (sharing is next), so you’ll help shape where it goes, not just execute a fixed roadmap.

Listen to the Suno version of this role! https://suno.com/s/GsrerPlrPvDQymS8

What You’ll Do

  • Lead a small team of fullstack product engineers who own Suno’s social layer — notifications, profiles, the follow graph, and social engagement from sharing to comments

  • Grow the team by hiring strong engineers, developing them across the stack, and holding a high bar through honest, firm performance management

  • Set technical direction for social systems at scale — guiding architecture for the follow graph, notifications, and profiles, and championing mobile-first API design

  • Partner with product, design, and data science on roadmap ideation, discovering and fostering the emergent social behaviors that deepen engagement

  • Ship retention-driving features with end-to-end rigor: metrics read-outs, logging, dogfooding, and post-launch follow-up

  • Advance Suno’s mission of making creative fulfillment a daily reality by building the network that lets people create and experience music together


What You’ll Need

Must-Haves

  • 5–7 years in software engineering, including 2–4 years managing engineers — hiring, developing, and running firm performance cycles

  • Genuine, demonstrable intuition for social products and network effects — you’re a real user and a first-principles thinker about what makes products sticky, and you understand how to grow a network without collapsing context

  • Enough technical depth to guide architecture and stay hands-on — you can review code, weigh trade-offs, and jump into the codebase when it helps

  • A track record of creating structure in ambiguous, 0→1 environments, ideally shipping consumer social products at startup pace

  • Strong asynchronous, cross-functional communicator who reduces ambiguity rather than creating it

  • A love of music (listening, exploring, making — we’re not picky about genre)

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience on a growth team — social and growth are two sides of the same coin

  • Founding or 0→1 experience inside a larger organization (a “startup within a startup”)

  • Fullstack range across mobile, web, and backend

  • Familiarity with network-effects and engagement-mechanics literature

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Additional Notes:

  • Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

  • This role requires working onsite at our NYC office.

Compensation:

  • The annual salary range for this role is $277K - $346K + target equity + benefits (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.title: Senior UX Researcher, Qualitative
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

Founded in 2023 by Harvard alumni with a shared passion for music, Suno has quickly grown to 250 employees while empowering more than 100 million people to create original songs. In 2026, we raised a $400 million Series D at a $5.4 billion valuation to continue building innovative products that amplify creativity and imagination.

About The Role

For most people, making music has always felt out of reach. Suno is changing that, and mobile is where that change will happen for the majority of people.

We are looking for a Senior Qualitative UX Researcher to own the deepest questions about the people we haven't reached yet. Not the users who already know what a stem is, but the ones who open the app with no idea what's possible and no vocabulary for what they want. Understanding how creative confidence gets built, across a very wide range of ages and levels of experience, is one of the highest-leverage research problems at the company right now.

You'll be the research partner to the PM and designer leading mobile create and working alongside them to address shared product questions. You’ll also collaborate with the researcher focused on rapid mobile evaluation, ensuring that usability insights and foundational research inform one another.

This is a senior individual contributor role with significant ownership. You’ll develop and advocate for the research roadmap, adapt it as priorities evolve, and confidently revise your perspective when new evidence emerges.


Listen to the song we made about this role! https://suno.com/s/Asd2doVRgxJzjenY

What You'll Do

Own the foundational research agenda for mobile create - Define and run the generative studies that shape where the product goes: ethnography, diary and longitudinal studies, in-context observation, concept work. Decide what's worth studying, and say no to what won't change a decision.

Go where the creating happens - Lead in-person and in-field research, including in-home sessions and sessions with more than one participant at once, such as household and family settings. Some of the most important behavior here will never show up in a remote unmoderated test.

Be a true partner, not a service desk - Sit with the mobile create PM, designer, and engineers as decisions are being made. Bring user signal early enough to change the shape of the work, not late enough to only validate it.

Turn findings into things the org keeps using - Segmentations, journey and jobs-to-be-done frameworks, opportunity maps, design principles that outlive any single launch and get cited in rooms you're not in.

Connect qual to the numbers - Pair depth with survey and behavioral data. Work with data science as a peer to size what you find, and with growth partners to translate insight into acquisition, onboarding, and retention bets.

Raise the craft bar - Mentor, review study designs, and unblock other researchers. This is an IC role with real influence, not a management track.

Who You Are

  • 5+ years of industry UX research experience, with deep specialization in qualitative methods and consumer mobile products

  • A track record of research that shifted strategy, not just UI. You can name the roadmap decisions, product bets, or reversals your work drove

  • Experience running in-person research with groups, including in-home and in-context sessions, sessions with more than one participant at a time, and the consent and assent workflows that come with them

  • Rigorous methodological judgment and the range to match method to question rather than reaching for the same study every time

  • Sound instincts about ethics and participant comfort with people who are not professional research subjects

  • Fluency with quantitative data. You can read an experiment readout, design a survey that holds up, and hold your own with a data scientist

  • Genuinely self-directed. You find the important question before anyone assigns it, and you have a high tolerance for ambiguity, shifting priorities, and moving faster than feels comfortable

  • The ability to influence senior stakeholders without authority, and to hold a position when the room disagrees

  • Excited by consumer products, creativity, music, and AI, and by the idea that the interaction patterns for this category don't exist yet

What You'll Need

  • Startup experience, especially as the first or only researcher, or as a founder (even with a research team around you, this role runs on ownership rather than process)

  • Experience in sensitive product areas such as safety, trust, or wellbeing

  • Background in consumer mobile in audio, music, or social

  • Experience researching AI and generative products, where user mental models are still forming

Nice to Haves

  • PhD in HCI, Human-Centered Computing, Psychology, Learning Sciences, or a related field, combined with real industry experience.

  • You know of a good UX research lab or in-person session space in LA that we could use, and bonus points if you've worked out of it

  • Bonus points if you've used Suno to make music

Additional Notes

  • You must be authorized to work in the United States

  • You must be willing to work 5 days per week at our Venice Beach office

  • Some travel for team meetings and field research

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Compensation

The annual salary range for this role is: $176K-$220K (before equity)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Connect qual to the numbers - Pair depth with survey and behavioral data. Work with data science as a peer to size what you find, and with growth partners to translate insight into acquisition, onboarding, and retention bets.

Raise the craft bar - Mentor, review study designs, and unblock other researchers. This is an IC role with real influence, not a management track.




WHO YOU ARE

 - 5+ years of industry UX research experience, with deep specialization in qualitative methods and consumer mobile products

 - A track record of research that shifted strategy, not just UI. You can name the roadmap decisions, product bets, or reversals your work drove

 - Experience running in-person research with groups, including in-home and in-context sessions, sessions with more than one participant at a time, and the consent and assent workflows that come with them

 - Rigorous methodological judgment and the range to match method to question rather than reaching for the same study every time

 - Sound instincts about ethics and participant comfort with people who are not professional research subjects

 - Fluency with quantitative data. You can read an experiment readout, design a survey that holds up, and hold your own with a data scientist

 - Genuinely self-directed. You find the important question before anyone assigns it, and you have a high tolerance for ambiguity, shifting priorities, and moving faster than feels comfortable

 - The ability to influence senior stakeholders without authority, and to hold a position when the room disagrees

 - Excited by consumer products, creativity, music, and AI, and by the idea that the interaction patterns for this category don't exist yet




WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - Startup experience, especially as the first or only researcher, or as a founder (even with a research team around you, this role runs on ownership rather than process)

 - Experience in sensitive product areas such as safety, trust, or wellbeing

 - Background in consumer mobile in audio, music, or social

 - Experience researching AI and generative products, where user mental models are still forming


NICE TO HAVES

 - PhD in HCI, Human-Centered Computing, Psychology, Learning Sciences, or a related field, combined with real industry experience. 

 - You know of a good UX research lab or in-person session space in LA that we could use, and bonus points if you've worked out of it

 - Bonus points if you've used Suno to make music



Additional Notes

 - You must be authorized to work in the United States

 - You must be willing to work 5 days per week at our Venice Beach office

About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About the role

You will own the operating floor of Trust & Safety at Suno: review queues, vendor capacity, quality programs, SLAs, and escalation workflows. Our enforcement system blends automated decisioning with human judgment, and your job is to make the human side of that system fast, accurate, and worth every dollar it costs. You will report to our Trust & Safety lead and work closely with Product, Eng, Legal, Comms, and the broader Operations team.

Listen to the song we made about the role: https://suno.com/s/bWZ30M98bvirsCPq

What you'll do

  • Run day-to-day enforcement operations: queue health, latency, SLA attainment and escalation handling across all content categories.

  • Own vendor and BPO performance: capacity forecasting, quality enforcement, contract performance and site management.

  • Build and run the training, QA, and calibration program that keeps decision quality measurable and improving.

  • Manage capacity planning against rapid volume growth, including the tradeoffs between headcount, vendor spend, and automation.

  • Define tooling requirements for reviewer workflows and partner with Engineering to ship them.

  • Support reviewer wellness and resilience programs for the teams doing the hardest work on the platform.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years in Trust & Safety, content moderation, or CX operations, including 2+ years directly managing reviewers or vendor teams.

  • Ownership of operational metrics you can speak to concretely: SLA attainment, queue latency, QA scores, cost per decision, reviewer utilization.

  • Hands-on vendor or BPO management with real performance accountability, not just relationship handling.

  • Experience building or running a QA and calibration program with measurable decision-quality outcomes.

Nice to have

  • Operating experience alongside ML-assisted enforcement: queue routing on model scores, human-in-the-loop workflows.

  • Reviewer wellness and resilience program exposure.

  • UGC or generative AI platform background.

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About the Role

We're looking for a Staff AI Security Engineer to secure how Suno's models are built, trained, and served, and to build the systems that keep them that way. You'll work across the full model lifecycle, from training pipelines and compute infrastructure to the products millions of people create with. You'll partner closely with ML research, platform, and product engineering, and set the technical direction for AI security as the function grows. There's a lot to build, and you'll be building it.

Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/JJoqlgtg8424Uq68

What You'll Do

  • Design and build security controls for model training and serving infrastructure, including compute clusters, pipelines, access to model artifacts, and the software supply chain behind them

  • Engineer detection, monitoring, and guardrail systems for model inputs, outputs, and agentic tool use, as production code rather than one-off scripts

  • Break our own systems through adversarial testing and red-teaming across models, pipelines, and products, then drive the fixes to done

  • Partner with ML research and platform teams to make secure defaults the easy path in how models are trained, evaluated, and deployed

  • Partner with product engineering to threat model and review customer-facing AI features before launch, and build the shared controls that let teams ship them safely by default

  • Set technical direction for AI security at Suno, including standards, reference architectures, and the roadmap, while raising the security bar across engineering

  • Help make creative fulfillment a daily reality for everyone by keeping the platform trustworthy enough that millions of people want to create on it

What You'll Need

  • 8–10 years in security engineering, including hands-on work securing ML systems or large-scale ML infrastructure in production

  • A track record of designing and shipping security systems and tooling, not only assessing them

  • Deep knowledge of cloud and infrastructure security: IAM, Kubernetes, network segmentation, secrets management, and infrastructure as code

  • Strong understanding of ML training and serving pipelines and their attack surface, including model supply chain risks and protecting model weights and artifacts

  • Fluency with LLM and generative AI attack vectors and frameworks such as OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and MITRE ATLAS

  • Strong coding skills in Python or Go

  • Experience setting technical direction and influencing senior engineers and leaders without formal authority

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience at a foundational model company or an AI research lab

  • Securing GPU compute environments or distributed training at scale

  • Hands-on use of adversarial testing tools such as Garak or PyRIT

  • Background securing audio, media, or other generative content pipelines

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

 

Compensation:

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. About the Role

We're looking for a Privacy Engineering Lead to build Suno's privacy and AI governance function from scratch. You'll set the technical direction for how we handle data and permissions across our platform, models, and agents — building the infrastructure that enforces policy at the point of use and verifies outcomes like retention and deletion. You'll partner closely with Legal and Product while hiring and growing your own engineering team to scale this work across the company.

Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/OXY6WfUr15oSP1UR

What You'll Do

  • Build the policy foundations for how Suno handles data, permitted uses, and AI, in partnership with Legal.

  • Own data discovery, classification, and permissions mapping across our product, analytics, and vendor systems.

  • Design and operate governance controls across our products, data platforms, models, and agents, enforcing consent, access, and data-sharing rules.

  • Lead verified user rights operations, including access, correction, deletion, and consent management, partnering with Product on self-service tools.

  • Hire and grow a dedicated privacy engineering team, giving this work the focused ownership it needs to scale.

  • Help make responsible data handling part of how Suno builds every new model and feature, in service of making creative fulfillment a daily reality for everyone.

What You'll Need

Must-Haves

  • 8-10 years hands-on software engineering experience, with the technical depth to help build and ship enforcement infrastructure yourself, not only define policy for others to implement.

  • Deep experience in privacy engineering or data governance, including working familiarity with regulatory frameworks like GDPR and CCPA.

  • Experience as an engineering manager who has maintained real technical depth, or as a Staff+ engineer ready to grow into people management.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with AI/ML governance, model evaluation pipelines, or generative AI systems.

  • Background at a consumer tech company at scale, or one with a significant European user base.

About the Role

Suno is looking for a Staff Technical Program Manager to help us scale our technical programs and launches - coordinating across engineering, product, and other functions to land some of our largest initiatives. As a Staff TPM, you’ll have the ability to create and drive programs, and partner with us to figure out where we should be investing that we aren’t today. TPM as a function is new to Suno, and there’s a real opportunity to help us build it from the ground up

What You'll Do

  • Lead cross-functional programs end to end — things like model launches, multi-team engineering efforts, and engineering initiatives — from scoping, through rollout, and tracking

  • Coach and grow the team's TPM, building the mentorship and structure that hasn't existed here before

  • Help shape what "TPM" means at Suno — the working model, the organizing principles, and where the function needs to grow

  • Partner closely with engineering leadership so cross-functional continues to move fast and collaboration is easy, contributing directly to team velocity

  • Help turn Suno's mission — making creative fulfillment a daily reality for everyone — into shipped, coordinated reality across teams

What You'll Need

Must-Haves

  • 8–10 years in program or technical program management

  • Demonstrated adaptability — you find the right approach for the environment you're in rather than importing what worked somewhere else

  • A clear, articulable framework for how you evaluate and measure whether a program is actually succeeding

  • Enough technical/coding fluency to get hands-on and understand the work that needs to be done, not just coordinate around it

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About the role

The Lead Corporate Security Engineer will be our domain expert for securing our Corporate IT environment. You’ll work closely with colleagues in IT, Business Systems, Security, and Engineering to ensure that our corporate systems are implemented and maintained securely. As a senior member of the team, your impact will be split between building your team, enabling others, and doing hands-on work to mature our systems, processes, and behaviors.

You'll lead the corporate security domain end to end: identity and access governance, endpoint and vulnerability management, detection and response, third-party integration risk, vendor assessment, and SaaS posture. You'll set the standard, own the roadmap, and be accountable for the outcome. IT Engineering runs the platforms day to day and are your closest partners.

Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/BiNdRVfLZRJXlfSW

How this role works with IT

Ownership splits by layer, not by system. IT Engineering owns the run; you own the standard and the direction.

  • You set the corporate security roadmap. What we secure, in what order, to what bar with buy-in from leadership and XFN stakeholders

  • IT engineering owns platform operations. Our SaaS portfolio is administered and integrated by them. You define what those platforms must enforce

  • You raise the bar around you. You make your reasoning explicit so that partners make good security calls without you in the room, and you build the tooling and defaults that make the secure path the default path

What you'll own

Identity and access governance

  • Own the access model at Suno: the RBAC and entitlement design, least-privilege defaults, and the governance layer in Lumos that enforces them

  • Set the standard for what access review, certification, and approval should look like here — then build toward it rather than importing someone else's framework

  • Drive access lifecycle automation so joiner/mover/leaver is correct by default and exceptions are visible

  • Get ahead of non-human identity: service accounts, agents, and automations are a growing share of what holds access at Suno, and we need a model for them before it's urgent

Endpoint security and vulnerability management

  • Own the security standard for our fleet: hardening baseline, compliance signals, device trust, and how endpoint posture feeds access decisions

  • Own third-party vulnerability management as a program — coverage, risk-based remediation SLAs, reporting, and the negotiation with teams whose tools are the problem

  • Partner with the IT engineer who owns Kandji so the standard becomes deployed policy without degrading how people work

Detection and response

  • Own our EDR deployment and maintenance

  • Collaborate with Detection and Response on corporate security incidents to closure

Third-party and integration risk

  • Own how Suno evaluates third-party access: integration and OAuth review for Slack, Google Workspace and the rest of the portfolio, plus vendor security assessment at purchase and renewal

  • Define our risk appetite in practice and make it legible enough that others apply it without you

  • Turn recurring decisions into policy, scope guidance, and tooling so the review queue shrinks as the company grows

SaaS security posture

  • Build and own the program: the bar for our SaaS applications, the assessment cadence, and the remediation that follows

  • Improve tenant-level configuration across the portfolio — SSO and SCIM coverage, MFA and session policy, admin role hygiene, OAuth grant and token management, data sharing defaults

Cross-functional leadership

  • Work with IT, Security, Engineering, AI Enablement, and Legal to shape how Suno builds and buys

  • Influence the scope of what comes next: how our GRC function plugs in, what we automate versus staff, where the next investment goes

  • Mentor and raise the technical bar for people around you, including partners who aren't security specialists

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: you've formed your own view of our security posture, built working relationships with the IT engineers the broader Security team, and told us the three things we're wrong about

  • First 6 months: a corporate security roadmap exists that IT and the CISO are aligned behind, with the sequencing and the tradeoffs made explicit; the highest-risk items are already moving

  • First year: entitlement sprawl and vulnerability backlog are measurably down, detection reflects our real risks, third-party review is fast enough that nobody routes around it, and the standard holds because it's built into tooling and shared judgment rather than into you

What you'll bring

  • ~8+ years in corporate/enterprise security or security engineering, including having owned identity, endpoint, or SaaS security as a domain rather than as a set of tickets

  • Deep hands-on expertise with a modern IdP and with IGA or access-governance tooling (Lumos, Veza, ConductorOne, Opal, or similar)

  • You've designed an entitlement or RBAC model across a large SaaS portfolio and lived with the consequences long enough to know what breaks

  • Endpoint security depth in a macOS-primary fleet: MDM-delivered hardening, compliance and device trust, third-party patch and vulnerability management at scale

  • Strong command of OAuth, SAML, OIDC, and SCIM, and of the risk model behind third-party integrations

  • A track record of setting a security standard that other people applied without you enforcing it — written policy, tooling, defaults, or all three

  • Experience influencing engineering and business teams who don't report to you, early enough in their process to change the outcome

  • Automation fluency: Python or TypeScript, REST APIs, and a habit of building integrations and internal tooling as a normal part of the job

  • Excellent writing and judgment under ambiguity. You can hold a position with an executive and change it when the evidence says to

  • A calibrated sense of risk and how to communicate likelihood, impact, and tradeoffs

Helpful, not required: insider risk or DLP programs, zero-trust network access, SOC 2 or ISO program ownership, just-in-time access patterns or identity-as-code, securing AI agent and non-human identity access, prior experience as the first or second security hire at a fast-growing company.

Work Location Policy

This role is expected to work from Suno's SF, NYC, or Cambridge, MA office 5 days a week, per Suno's company policy. Full-time employees will receive competitive equity packages, and comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered may vary depending on location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

Additional Notes

Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

Willingness to travel (up to 25%) to lead team members and support offices across Suno locations, with a deliberate cadence in Cambridge and NYC during the first six months.

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

About the Role

We’re looking for early members of our machine learning recommendations team. You’ll work closely with the founding team and have ownership of a wide variety of technical decisions on how we build and deploy our state of the art recommendation models.

Check out the Suno version of the job here! https://suno.com/s/ujpqmS3Rf9Qg911A

What You’ll Do

  • Formulate and develop mathematical models of user preference, similarity, and engagement for music discovery

  • Design learning systems that infer user taste from sparse, noisy, and evolving interaction data

  • Build and deploy scalable recommendation and ranking models that operate under real-time latency and throughput constraints

  • Translate abstract objectives (relevance, novelty, diversity, long-term satisfaction) into measurable metrics and optimized systems

  • Run large-scale experiments and causal analyses to evaluate model behavior and product impact

  • Work closely with product and research leadership to define the technical direction of Suno’s personalization systems

What You’ll Need

  • Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience

  • Proficiency in Python and modern ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch) with the ability to implement and iterate on research ideas

  • Solid knowledge and understanding of data pipelines and cloud technologies, e.g., Spark, AWS, etc.

  • Proven track record of building, deploying, and maintaining 0->1 production Machine Learning or Data Science solutions

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills working with cross-functional teams such as Product, Data, Infra, etc.

  • A love of music (listening, exploring, or making) is a strong plus

    Preferred Qualifications:

    • 3+ years of industrial experience in Recommendation, Search, Ads, Optimization, Reinforcement Learning, or related disciplines

    • Publications at top Machine Learning, Data Mining, Information Retrieval, Natural Language Processing conferences such as KDD, ICML, NeurIPS, RecSys, ACL, etc.

jobs.title: Staff Security GRC Analyst
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About the Role

We're looking for a Staff Security GRC Analyst to build Suno's security compliance program from the ground up. You'll report to our CISO, work alongside our AppSec and InfraSec teams, and own the control framework that ties everything together: which controls we have, how they map to SOC 2 and NIST CSF, and whether they actually work. You're as comfortable reading a cloud config as an audit standard, and you'd rather automate evidence collection with AI than chase screenshots. It's a greenfield build with real stakes and a direct line to leadership.

Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/8U6fbhqLEghsnRsm

What You'll Do

  • Build and own Suno's security control framework, mapping controls to SOC 2, NIST CSF, and future frameworks, and writing control descriptions with the teams who run them.

  • Lead SOC 2 preparation end to end, from gap assessments and readiness tracking to driving remediation with control owners and working with our external auditor.

  • Automate evidence collection and control monitoring with scripts, integrations, and AI tools, deciding where human review stays in the loop.

  • Run vendor security reviews, keep our security policies current, and answer customer security questionnaires alongside Product and Legal.

  • Partner with the CISO to give leadership and the board a clear, evidence-backed view of our security posture, and lay the foundations of GRC as part of a growing Security team.

  • Help earn the trust of the partners and customers who bring Suno to more people, so creating music can be part of everyone's day.

What You'll Need

Must-Haves

  • 7–9 years in GRC, security compliance, or IT audit.

  • Hands-on, end-to-end ownership of a security compliance program as its primary owner, ideally including taking a company through its first SOC 2.

  • Deep working knowledge of SOC 2 and NIST CSF, including control mapping, audit mechanics (design vs. operating effectiveness, sampling, evidence), and staying current as requirements evolve.

  • Enough technical fluency to read a cloud configuration, access setup, or pipeline and judge whether it enforces what the control says. You don't need to write production code.

  • Comfort building your own automation with scripts or AI tools.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience standing up continuous controls monitoring or automated evidence collection, including what it covered and what changed as a result.

  • Experience applying LLMs to assurance work, such as control drafting, framework mapping, or evidence testing.

  • Experience with cloud environments such as AWS or GCP, and with a modern GRC platform.

  • Certifications such as CISA, CISSP, or CRISC.

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. About the Role

Lead the team that keeps Suno Corporate IT Systems running. As Senior Manager, IT Operations, you'll lead our IT Engineers and build our IT Service Desk. Your team owns IT operations across our four US offices — Cambridge, New York, San Francisco, and Los Angeles — including identity and access management, endpoint management, collaboration software, office A/V, office networking, and Tailscale.

Your success will be measured through the impact of your team. You'll establish clear ownership over operational areas, ensure top-notch service that your colleagues trust, and your team will leverage AI and Automation to scale efficiently. You'll partner closely with Operations, People, Finance, Security, and Engineering, and you'll be the senior IT presence on the West Coast.

Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/0fzLoGLLVcxm3uBA

What Your Team Owns

  • Identity and access management — Okta, SSO and SCIM coverage, joiner / mover / leaver automation via our IGA platform, access reviews, and ad hoc access requests.

  • Endpoint management — the Mac fleet in MDM, zero-touch enrollment, OS and patch compliance, device trust, and endpoint security in partnership with our EDR/MDR providers.

  • Collaboration software — Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, and the broader SaaS portfolio: configuration, hardening, licensing, and lifecycle.

  • Office A/V — conference rooms, videoconferencing, and event spaces.

  • Corporate Networking — wired, wireless, and WAN across four sites, including design for buildouts and expansions with outside experts where it makes sense.

  • Tailscale — our zero-trust network layer: ACL policy, device posture, access to internal tools and infrastructure, and the day-to-day administration in collaboration with Engineering

  • IT service delivery — the service desk, AI IT Service Management platform, SLAs, escalation paths, knowledge base, and the Tier 0 partnership with office managers.

What You'll Do

  • Manage the IT Engineers — set expectations against our role standards, give direct feedback, run 1:1s and performance conversations, and grow people on the IC track. Manage against outcomes and impact, not tenure and activities.

  • Build the IT Help Desk — define the service model (what the desk handles, what escalates to engineering, what office managers cover at Tier 0), write the job profiles, our our service desk team.

  • Own operational outcomes — the team's quarterly plan across the areas above, clear ownership of each area by a named engineer, and honest status reporting to the Senior Manager of IT and leadership.

  • Run change well — size changes by scope, impact, and reversibility; make sure the team communicates before changes land and can roll them back after; bring in the right partners early and avoid surprises.

  • Scale service as Suno scales — runbooks and knowledge articles good enough for AI-powered self-service to actually deflect; automate what the team has handled twice; absorb headcount growth without proportional growth in tickets or effort.

  • Manage vendors and partners — MSPs, network and A/V integrators, EDR/MDR providers, and SaaS vendors; hold them to results and know when to bring work in-house.

  • Lead IT for the West Coast — own IT for the SF office directly, oversee LA coverage, and partner with Facilities on buildouts, moves, and expansions.

What You'll Need

Must-Haves

  • 10+ years in IT, including 3+ years managing IT engineers, a help desk, or an IT operations team at a high-growth company.

  • You've built a support function, not just inherited one — you can discuss service model, SLAs, staffing, and deflection you put in place and what changed because of it.

  • Working knowledge across the stack your team owns — identity (Okta or equivalent, SCIM, IGA), Apple-first endpoint management, Google Workspace and Slack administration, office networking and A/V, and zero-trust networking (Tailscale or comparable) — deep enough to set priorities, review your team's work credibly, and ask the right questions, without needing to be the best engineer in the room.

  • Strong people leadership — you've hired, coached, given hard feedback, and managed performance, including for people in other offices and time zones.

  • Clear written communication — you need to be able to communicate clearly and concisely for executive, business, and technical audiences.

  • Judgment under growth — you can tell a one-way door from a two-way door, move fast on the reversible, and slow down on the consequential.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Hands-on background with Okta, SCIM provisioning, and IGA tooling (Lumos, SailPoint, Saviynt, or comparable).

  • Modern Apple MDM (Iru, Jamf, Jumpcloud) and endpoint security partnerships (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Expel, or similar).

  • Tailscale or another zero-trust network layer in production — ACL design, device posture, SSO integration.

  • ITSM design experience — intake, categorization, SLAs, and reporting from scratch; AI-powered self-service a plus.

  • Experience running IT through a multi-office expansion — new sites, floor expansions, and the integrators and vendors that come with them.

  • Experience as an early IT leader at a company that grew from hundreds to a thousand employees.

Work Location Policy

This role is expected to work from the San Francisco Suno office 5 days a week, per Suno's company policy. Full-time employees will receive competitive equity packages, and comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered may vary depending on location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

Additional Notes

Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

Willingness to travel (up to 25%) to lead team members and support offices across Suno locations, with a deliberate cadence in Cambridge and NYC during the first six months.

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave
